summary.headline: Vidya Wires FY26 revenue rose 24.2% to INR 18,396.4 mn and PAT reached INR 576.1 mn; ALCU plant began production on 7 Feb 2026.
summary.overview: FY26 revenue from operations was INR 18,396.4 mn (+24.2% YoY), EBITDA INR 857.8 mn at a 4.66% margin (+35 bps), and PAT INR 576.1 mn. Management said FY26 volume was about 18,024 MT (+6.5%), with revenue growth of roughly 17-18% on a volume basis, and Q4 revenue grew 58%, which management attributed mainly to higher copper prices and better utilisation. ALCU Industries, the wholly owned subsidiary, started manufacturing on 7 Feb 2026 and contributed about 800 MT in FY26; it is in a phased ramp-up with about 6,000 MT installed and 8,000-9,000 MT more due by Sep-Oct 2026 (before Diwali). Management also flagged working capital at about 60 days, which it aims to bring to 50-52 days, and debtors of 41 days targeted to about 35 days.

financial_highlights.change: YoY, per analyst question; management did not dispute

segments.name: Power and transmission
segments.commentary: About 51% of revenue, per management; includes transformer-related products. Management said this segment performed well.

segments.name: Renewable and EV
segments.commentary: About 7% of revenue; new PV round ribbon and aluminium products are aimed at this segment.

segments.name: Copper vs aluminium (revenue mix)
segments.commentary: About 96% copper and 4% aluminium as of March 2026; management expects roughly 90:10 over time, though it said the mix cannot be fixed given copper volatility.

segments.name: ALCU Industries (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Manufacturing began 7 Feb 2026 with about 800 MT in FY26; new products include aluminium paper-covered conductors, aluminium enamelled wires and strips, PV round ribbon, multi-paper covered copper conductors and copper bus bars. CTC contribution is zero until about Sep-Oct 2026.

guidance_outlook: ALCU capacity to reach about 35,000-36,000 MT total by Diwali (Sep-Oct 2026), from about 19,000 MT currently planned in the expansion; management said full operation at 36,000 MT in FY28.
FY27 utilisation of the new ~18,000 MT ALCU capacity expected at 50-60%; optimum utilisation is about 80% of installed capacity, expected in FY28.
EBITDA per MT expected to improve in FY27 on new product mix; management declined to commit to a INR 66/MT peer benchmark.
Export mix target of 75% domestic and 25% export; exports currently about 12% of volume.
Working capital target: cycle to 50-52 days from 60; debtors to about 35 days from 41; inventory to remain about 21-23 days.
Management gave no quantitative FY27 revenue or margin guidance, saying only that growth would be good and new capacity would add to it.
Gujarat GST-linked subsidy expected to cover 45-50% of investment over 10 years for the new unit.
capex_capacity: Expansion from about 19,000 MT to about 36,000 MT planned; about 6,000 MT installed by the call and 8,000-9,000 MT more by Sep-Oct 2026, with full build before December 2026 per one answer.
CTC (copper transposed conductor) Phase 1 capacity of about 3,000 TPA, with commencement expected Sep-Oct 2026 (before Diwali); CTC contribution is currently zero.
Land is available to expand capacity further at the existing site, per management.
Management said it will announce any further capex when the board approves it; no new capex plan beyond the current expansion was stated.
Capex from IPO proceeds is being phased in line with operational readiness; exact amounts were not disclosed on the call.
demand_pricing: Management said copper and aluminium price moves have little margin impact because the model is back-to-back hedged on LME; minor shifts only.
Standard customer credit period is 30-45 days; dispatch typically 20-25 days after order.
Q4 revenue growth attributed to higher copper prices over the prior 5-6 months, plus better utilisation in the seasonally stronger quarter.

Competition: peers named as Precision Wires, Ram Ratna Wires and KSH International, with about 50-60% product overlap. Management expects market share to rise from 5.7% to 11.3% post-expansion per investor slide.
CTC demand in India estimated at 30,000-40,000 tons, growing faster; international demand cited as large.

Import share of raw materials stated at about 40-50%, kept balanced with domestic sourcing; ocean freight and packing costs have risen, but supply has not been materially impacted (only one Middle East supplier affected).
Management said 35-40% of the plant has product fungibility.

qa_highlights.question: Volume and ALCU contribution in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 volume about 18,024 MT (+6.5%). ALCU contributed about 800 MT from early Feb 2026; about 6,000 MT capacity installed, with 8,000-9,000 MT more by Sep-Oct.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of copper and aluminium prices on margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said back-to-back hedging on LME means price moves have only marginal impact on margins.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital and OCF conversion?
qa_highlights.answer: Working cycle is 60 days, targeted at 50-52 days by lengthening creditor days and cutting debtor days. Inventory at 20-23 days is in line with requirements.

qa_highlights.question: Inventory build and cash flow outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said historical inventory is 21-24 days, there was no inventory build at year-end, and it expects to stay around 21 days.

qa_highlights.question: Why not use letters of credit to extend payables?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it gets better interest rates on CC facilities given its CRISIL rating, and LCs add documentation and time.

qa_highlights.question: Exports and margin differential?
qa_highlights.answer: Exports are about 12% of volume against a 25% target; management said export margins are always better than domestic.

risks_watch: ALCU ramp-up execution: 8,000-9,000 MT still to be added by Sep-Oct 2026, and FY27 utilisation expected at only 50-60%.
Working capital conversion: OCF has lagged EBITDA over the last three years; the 60-day cycle needs to fall to 50-52 days.
Other expenses rose sequentially from about INR 28 mn to INR 83 mn in Q4; management attributed this to one-off items not previously expensed and said costs will track revenue going forward.
Freight and packing cost inflation linked to the Middle East conflict; management said it has not been material so far.
Competitive capacity additions by peers as the market grows, with management stating its multi-product mix offers protection.
Q4 volume and Q4 FY25 comparatives were not given on the call; management said they would be shared separately.
Management could not give quantified EBITDA/MT or margin guidance for the new products.
summary.management_tone: Confident on structural demand and the new capacity, but cautious and vague on quantification: it declined to give FY27 revenue or margin guidance, product-level margins and Q4 volumes. Answers were often repeated or deferred to later disclosure.
key_quotes: We believe in growth through efficiency.
By design, we are not yet at full capacity.
So basically, there were some expenses which we had not considered. They have been expensed out in this quarter.
So our EBITDA per metric ton we expect to be better in this financial year.

growth.why: No numeric FY27 revenue guidance; management only said it will maintain 'good growth', backed by ALCU capacity rising from ~6,000 MT installed toward ~35,000-36,000 MT by Sep-Oct 2026 with FY27 utilisation of the new ~18,000 MT at 50-60%.
